title: The Java ArrayList.remove() overload trap
description:
List in Java has two remove methods: remove(Object) and remove(int index). With a list of Integer, calling list.remove(1) runs the by-index overload and deletes the element at position 1 -- not the value 1. This Short shows the unambiguous String-list case first, then the Integer gotcha and the Integer.valueOf fix.

Source lesson(s):
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-1/05-arrays-collections/

beats.narration: Here's a Java trick question. You've got a list of numbers, you call remove with the number one, and the wrong element vanishes. Why?
With a list of strings, it's unambiguous. Remove Call Sam by value, then remove index zero by position. List has two remove methods, and Java picks based on the argument type.
Now switch to a list of Integers. Call remove with a plain int, and Java runs the remove-by-index overload. It drops the element at that position, not the value you wanted.
To actually remove the value one, box it yourself: remove Integer dot valueOf one. Same method name, completely different behavior.
